Attack vector # Stored XSS via Unsanitised SVG Uploads Moderate niwinz published GHSA-xg6f-5v5x-g4w2 Sep 25, 2026 ## Affected versions <=2.16.0 ## Patched versions 2.18.0 ## Description ### Summary Penpot allows authenticated users with file edit permissions to upload SVG media. SVGs are stored without sanitising active content and served from the Penpot origin as `image/svg+xml`. A malicious SVG can execute JavaScript when opened directly, allowing authenticated same-origin requests as the victim. ### Details `image/svg+xml` is accepted as a valid media type. The backend parses SVGs for basic root/dimension validation, but does not remove ` Loading profile... ### Impact An attacker who can upload media can create a stored same-origin XSS payload. If a victim opens the SVG asset while authenticated, attacker-controlled JavaScript can read data and perform actions available to the victim through Penpot API/RPC endpoints. `HttpOnly` cookies do not prevent this because the browser still sends them on same-origin requests. ### Severity Moderate 6.8 # CVSS overall score This score calculates overall vulnerability severity from 0 to 10 and is based on the Common Vulnerability Scoring System (CVSS). / 10 #### CVSS v3 base metrics Attack vector Network Attack complexity Low Privileges required Low User interaction Required Scope Changed Confidentiality High Integrity None Availability None CVSS:3.1/AV:N/AC:L/PR:L/UI:R/S:C/C:H/I:N/A:N ### CVE ID CVE-2026-105694 ### Weaknesses Weakness CWE-79 #### Improper Neutralization of Input During Web Page Generation ('Cross-site Scripting') The product does not neutralize or incorrectly neutralizes user-controllable input before it is placed in output that is used as a web page that is served to other users. Attack vector # Stored XSS via SVG file upload on the /view endpoint High mattmillerai published GHSA-rj8c-c4p8-3c5h Jul 15, 2026 ## Package ComfyUI (pip) ## Affected versions < 0.28.0 ## Patched versions 0.28.0 ## Description ### Summary The `/view` endpoint served uploaded SVG files inline because `image/svg+xml` was missing from its dangerous-Content-Type blocklist, allowing stored XSS. ### Details `/view`'s blocklist forced `application/octet-stream` for HTML/JS/CSS but omitted `image/svg+xml`, and it did not set `Content-Disposition: attachment`. An attacker uploads (unauthenticated by default, e.g. via `/upload/image`) a malicious SVG carrying inline ` Step 2: Login and upload the malicious SVG as device image: # Login curl -c cookie.txt -X POST "http:///api/session" \ -H "Content-Type: application/x-www-form-urlencoded" \ -d "email=user@example.com&password=password" 3. Data Theft: Execute arbitrary JavaScript to access and exfiltrate sensitive data visible to the victim. 4. Persistent Attack: The malicious payload is stored on the server and executes whenever any user views the device (in device list, device details, etc.). 5. Phishing: Redirect users to fake login pages to capture credentials. Attack Scenario: 1. Attacker creates/modifies a device they have access to 2. Attacker uploads malicious SVG as device image 3. Admin or other users view the device (in dashboard, device list, etc.) 4. JavaScript executes in victim's browser context 5. Attacker receives victim's session cookie via their server 6. Attacker uses stolen session to access victim's account ## Suggested Fix ### Option 1: Disallow SVG Uploads (Recommended) Remove SVG from the allowed image types: private String imageExtension(String type) { return switch (type) { case "image/jpeg" -> "jpg"; case "image/png" -> "png"; case "image/gif" -> "gif"; -------------------------------------------------------------------------------- Stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) via Unsanitized SVG Attachment Upload Leading to Token Exposure · Advisory · go-vikunja/vikunja · GitHub (https://github.com/go-vikunja/vikunja/security/advisories/GHSA-7jp5-298q-jg98) 【turn292845search9】 [wordlim: 200] Published: 8 months ago; Crawled: 2 months ago; # Stored Cross-Site Scripting (XSS) via Unsanitized SVG Attachment Upload Leading to Token Exposure ... * Implement a strict Content Security Policy (CSP) to block script execution within uploaded files. ...
